correctness.rationale: First-step strong-Markov recursion gives \(m_v=2s_v-1\) and \(q_v=\sum_cq_c+2m_v^2-(h+1)\). This implies \(V_x=4s(s-1)+8\sum_{v\ne x}s_v(s_v-1)\). The lower bound follows from the nonnegative fringe terms and strict balancing of integer child sizes. The upper bound is proved by induction using \(F(t)=8(t^3-t)/3\), with strictly increasing first differences \(8t(t+1)\). Each equality case follows from a strict step. The proof covers all integers \(1\le k\le s-1\). Standalone exact rational finite checks passed for all rooted forms of unlabelled trees through order eight; those checks do not substitute for the induction.

value.rationale: For a fixed side-size, first-step root degree and common mean, the theorem provides an exact natural extremal classification with all equality cases. The matching-order, matching-marked-degree examples exhibit a variance ratio growing as \(m/6\), demonstrating that the dispersion is not controlled by mean and immediate branching alone. This directly relates to tree hitting-time nonconcentration rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
